messages.subject: Overlaying two stacked bar plots
parts:
Hi all,

I have the following code as example:

library(reshape);
library(reshape2);
library(ggplot2);
library(plyr);
library(grid);

df <- data.frame ( grp = rep ( c ('A', 'B') , each = 20 ),
                 Y1 = runif (40) ,
                 Y2 = runif (40) )

df2 <- data.frame ( grp = rep ( c('A', 'B'), each = 20 ),
                  Y1 = runif (40) ,
                  Y2 = runif (40) )

melted.df <- melt ( df, id='grp' )
melted.df2 <- melt ( df2, id='grp' )

mean.df <- ddply ( melted.df, .(variable, grp), summarize, mean=mean(value) )
mean.df2 <- ddply( melted.df2, .(variable, grp), summarize, mean=mean(value) )

Plot.1 <- ggplot ( NULL, aes(x = variable, y = mean) )  +
  geom_bar ( data=mean.df, aes(fill=grp), stat="identity" ) +
  scale_fill_grey() + theme_bw()
  
Plot.2 <- ggplot ( NULL, aes(x = variable, y = mean))  +
  geom_bar (data=mean.df2, aes(fill=grp), stat="identity") +
  scale_fill_grey() + theme_bw()


Two stacked bar plots were generated, let's say, one related to population data and the other related to sample data. I want to create a comparison between both by overlaying them, in such way that Y1 from Plot.1 is displayed by the side of Y1 from Plot.2, and so on.

How that could be handled? I cannot change the type of graph, I need to represent my data using stacked bar plots because I have proportions which summed is equal to one.

Thanks in advance for your attention,
